name: Charred Calamari “Aegean Ember”
description: A Michelin-level calamari starter featuring binchotan-charred squid, smoked squid consommé, preserved lemon gel, black garlic emulsion, and squid ink rice lace crisp with dramatic fine-dining presentation.
headnote: Scoring the squid in a crosshatch before curing it briefly in salt and sugar solves the two problems calamari usually has: the cuts help it curl into an appealing shape over the coals instead of seizing flat, and the short cure firms the flesh just enough that binchotan's high, dry heat chars the surface before the inside overcooks and turns rubbery.
keywords: calamari, squid, fine dining, michelin, seafood starter, molecular gastronomy, charred seafood

steps.instruction: Score the inside of the squid tubes in a crosshatch pattern without cutting through completely.
Mix sea salt, sugar, and lemon zest. Lightly cure squid for 20 minutes in the refrigerator.
Rinse squid gently and pat completely dry.
Prepare smoked squid consommé
Prepare preserved lemon gel
Prepare black garlic emulsion
Prepare squid ink rice lace crisp
Brush squid lightly with olive oil and grill over extremely hot binchotan charcoal for 45–60 seconds per side until lightly blistered.
Melt cultured butter with squid ink and glaze the grilled calamari immediately after cooking.
Rest calamari for 1 minute before slicing into elegant ribbons.
Plate smoked consommé reduction in the center of matte black stoneware.
Arrange calamari ribbons and tentacles vertically for height and movement.
Add dots of preserved lemon gel and swipes of black garlic emulsion.
Insert rice lace crisp shards for texture and architecture.
Finish with herb oil, finger lime pearls, bronze fennel, edible flowers, and Maldon salt.

winePairings.name: Grower Champagne Blanc de Blancs
winePairings.notes: High acidity and minerality balance the smoke and richness of the calamari.

winePairings.name: Santorini Assyrtiko
winePairings.notes: Saline and citrus-driven wine complements squid ink and preserved lemon.

steps.instruction: Roast squid trimmings until deeply caramelized.
Add shallot and garlic, then deglaze with vermouth.
Add fish stock and kombu and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Add bonito flakes and steep for 3 minutes.
Strain through a fine chinois.
Cold smoke using a smoking gun under a cloche for 1 minute.
Blend preserved lemon, water, and sugar until smooth.
Whisk in agar agar and boil for 30 seconds.
Set in a shallow tray until firm.
Blend again until glossy and smooth, then transfer to squeeze bottle.
Blend egg yolk, Dijon mustard, and black garlic until smooth.
Slowly stream in grapeseed oil until emulsified.
Finish with sherry vinegar and season lightly.
Pass through a fine sieve for an ultra-smooth finish.
Whisk rice flour, water, squid ink, and nori powder together until smooth.
Pour a very thin layer into a lightly oiled nonstick pan over medium-high heat.
Allow mixture to bubble aggressively until a lacy structure forms.
Cook until crisp and carefully transfer to paper towel.
